items_all.summary: A new real-world test puts AI coding agents in a simulated developer job with colleagues, project boards, and incomplete handoffs, where they have to keep developing software on their own and reliably close open tickets in a messy daily workflow. Even Opus 5.5 and Astra fall far short, solving fewer than one in ten tasks completely. The models finish clear, standalone assignments quickly, but they lose track as autonomous developers. items_all.title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
items_all.summary: The Lean and Mathlib community has officially confirmed Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis as correct. Dozens of independent verifiers checked the 17 million lines of computer code. The solution arrived years earlier than expected: Terence Tao had predicted it wouldn't happen until around 2050 and didn't expect AI to solve it alone. The article Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct appeared first on The Decoder .

items_all.title: A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels
items_all.summary: TensorLean, from Columbia University and CertiK, formally verifies production GPU kernels at the PTX level using Lean. It checked 149 kernel instances, proved 83 correct, and found 38 bugs in FlashAttention, DeepGEMM and more. The post A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all.summary_zh: 來自哥倫比亞大學與 CertiK 的 TensorLean，使用 Lean 在 PTX 層級對正式環境的 GPU 核心進行形式化驗證。它檢查了 149 個核心例項，證明瞭 83 個正確，並在 FlashAttention、DeepGEMM 等專案中發現了 38 個錯誤。

items_all_raw.summary: TensorLean, from Columbia University and CertiK, formally verifies production GPU kernels at the PTX level using Lean. The post A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels appeared first on MarkTechPost .
